title: One of four tests fails: hardcoded /books/1 breaks because DELETE does not reset AUTOINCREMENT
evidence: test_coverage=0.75 in scores.json (scorer = Surefire pass rate = 3/4). src/test/java/com/example/books/BookApiTest.java:22 clearDatabase() runs `DELETE FROM books` in @BeforeEach, which does NOT reset the SQLite AUTOINCREMENT id sequence in the shared in-memory DB (@SpringBootTest, cache=shared). The two id-dependent tests assume id==1: createsListsFiltersAndReadsBook (line 29, get /books/1) and updatesAndDeletesBook (lines 33-36, insert then put/delete /books/1). Whichever runs second sees id>=2, so its /books/1 calls 404 and the test fails.
suggestion: Do not hardcode id 1. Either reset the sequence per-test (DELETE FROM sqlite_sequence WHERE name='books', or DROP/recreate the table in @BeforeEach), or capture the id returned by POST/INSERT and use it in subsequent requests.

title: Tests are coupled through a shared in-memory DB and depend on JUnit method order
evidence: src/test/java/com/example/books/BookApiTest.java:15 uses one shared in-memory SQLite DB (jdbc:sqlite:file:books-test?mode=memory&cache=shared) for all methods with no @TestMethodOrder; state leaks between methods via the AUTOINCREMENT sequence, so the pass/fail outcome depends on which id-dependent test JUnit happens to run first.
suggestion: Isolate tests: give each method a fresh schema (recreate table in @BeforeEach) or a per-method DB, and assert against ids returned by the API rather than assumed values.
